answer.text: The company's ability to pay dividends
The company's ability to service its interest obligations from operating profits
The average interest rate on bank deposits
The ratio of current assets to current liabilities

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook uses EBIT to assess the company's ability to meet its annual interest and financial expenses, and defines the Interest Coverage Ratio as EBIT divided by Interest Expense, showing earnings relative to the interest obligation. The Trap: Dividend-paying ability, deposit interest rates and the current ratio describe different concepts and do not relate EBIT to interest cost. Note: Based on NISM Series XV workbook pp.160 and 173; the workbook only states that a ratio below one or negative means earnings are below interest or negative.
